key_insight: Weld quality in FFF-printed thermoplastics depends on coupled processing, material, and printed-structure effects—not simply higher energy input.
engineering_relevance: Welding can enable assemblies beyond printer build-volume limits, but reliable joints require coordinated printing and joining design.
method: Critically reviews six welding techniques for FFF-printed thermoplastics.
Examines joining mechanisms, process parameters, mechanical performance, and failure.
Connects polymer type, infill, porosity, and interface design to joint integrity.
evidence_signal: The reviewed evidence links joint quality to interacting process and structural factors, but differences in specimens and testing limit direct comparisons between techniques.
watch_item: Excessive heating can degrade or deform parts; evidence for microwave-assisted welding of separately printed components remains limited.
paper_title: Welding of thermoplastics printed by fused filament fabrication: A critical review of joining mechanisms and relationships between processing, structure, and properties
